extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic number theory
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook material on class field theory and complex multiplication, including definitions, fundamental theorems (Artin reciprocity, Takagi existence, Čebotarev), id`elic formulation, ring and Hilbert class fields, and properties of modular functions and the j-invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.18 (imaginary quadratic fields with class number 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Let K be an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant dK. Then h(dK) = 1 ⇔ dK = −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −19, −43, −67, −163. (ii) Let D ≡ 0, 1 mod 4, D < 0. Then h(D) = 1 ⇔ D = −3, −4, −7, −8, −11, −12, −19, −27, −28, −43, −67, −163.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classifies fundamental (part (i)) and general negative discriminants (part (ii)) with class number one; the text proves the reduction (i)⇒(ii) here and defers the full proof of (i) to later sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of decomposition and inertia groups
rubrics_metrics.description: For L/K Galois and B a prime of OL: DB = {σ ∈ Gal(L/K) : σ(B) = B}; IB = {σ ∈ Gal(L/K) : σ(a) = a mod B for all a ∈ OL}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to describe local Galois action at primes; these groups control ramification and residue action. Finite primes are called finite places; infinite embeddings are infinite primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ramification and ramification index
rubrics_metrics.description: Given p a finite prime of K and Bi primes of L above p, pOL = Π Bi^{ei} where ei ∈ Z>0 is the ramification index of Bi. p is ramified if some ei>1 and unramified otherwise; totally ramified if only one Bi lies above p with inertial degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: infinite prime of K is ramified in L if a real embedding becomes complex in L; extension L/K is unramified if unramified at all finite and infinite primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 3.2 (existence of Frobenius element for unramified primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L/K is Galois and p is a prime of OK unramified in L and B a prime of OL over p, there exists a unique σ ∈ Gal(L/K) such that σ(a) ≡ a^{N(p)} mod B for all a ∈ OL, where N(p) = |OK/p|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This σ is the Frobenius substitution at B; its conjugacy class depends only on p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.3 (Frobenius element / conjugacy class Frob_p)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unique σ of Lemma 3.2 is denoted (L/K over B) (Frob_B^{L/K}); the conjugacy class of these elements for primes over p is denoted Frob_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In abelian extensions the Frobenius conjugacy class is a single element, so one can regard Frob_p as an element of Gal(L/K). One extends multiplicatively to fractional ideals via Froba = Π (Frob_{pi})^{ai}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of modulus and generalized ideal class groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A modulus m for number field K is a formal product m = Π p^{n_p} over finite and infinite primes with constraints n_p ∈ Z_{\ge 0}, n_p = 0 or 1 for real infinite primes, n_p = 0 for complex infinite primes. I^m_K denotes fractional ideals coprime to m; P^m_{K,1} generated by principal ideals (α) with α ≡ 1 mod m0 and σ(α)>0 at real primes dividing m∞. A subgroup H with P^m_{K,1} ⊂ H ⊂ I^m_K gives quotient I^m_K/H a generalized ideal class group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In imaginary quadratic fields a modulus is just an ideal. These generalized class groups correspond to Galois groups of abelian extensions via the Artin map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin map (local/global definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For abelian extension L/K and modulus m divisible by ramified primes, the Artin map Φ_m : I^m_K → Gal(L/K) sends prime p (coprime to m) to Frob_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends multiplicatively to all ideals in I^m_K. Central object relating ideal-theoretic objects to Galois automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.6 (Artin reciprocity theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L/K be abelian and m a modulus divisible at least by all ramified primes. (i) The Artin map Φ_m is surjective. (ii) For sufficiently large exponents in m, ker(Φ_m) is a congruence subgroup for m, and I^m_K / ker Φ_m ≅ Gal(L/K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies Gal(L/K) as a generalized ideal class group for modulus m; surjectivity is a key reciprocity statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example 3.7 (Artin map for cyclotomic fields Q(ζ_m))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Q(ζ_m)/Q with modulus m∞ dividing all ramified primes, Φ_m : I^m_Q → Gal(Q(ζ_m)/Q) ≅ (Z/mZ)^* maps a/b ∈ I^m_Q with gcd(a,b)=1 to [a][b]^{-1} in (Z/mZ)^*, and ker Φ_m = P^m_{Q,1}. Frob_p corresponds to p mod m in (Z/mZ)^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete description showing Artin map generalizes classical residue class reciprocity modulo m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.8 (Takagi Existence Theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given modulus m of K and congruence subgroup H with P^m_{K,1} ⊂ H ⊂ I^m_K, there exists a unique abelian extension L/K (ramified only at primes dividing m) such that H = ker(Φ_m) for the Artin map Φ_m of L/K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the converse to Artin reciprocity: every generalized ideal class group arises from a unique abelian extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert class field construction and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Takagi with modulus m=1 and H = P(OK) gives a unique unramified abelian extension L/K (the Hilbert class field) with Gal(L/K) ≅ Cl(OK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hilbert class field is the maximal unramified abelian extension; every unramified abelian extension of K is contained in it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.9 (Hilbert class field is maximal unramified abelian extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hilbert class field L is the maximal unramified abelian extension of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, any unramified abelian extension of K lies inside L; degree [L:K] = h(OK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.11 (Artin reciprocity for the Hilbert class field)
rubrics_metrics.description: For L the Hilbert class field of K, the Artin map Φ : I(OK) → Gal(L/K) is surjective with kernel exactly principal ideals P(OK), hence Cl(OK) ≅ Gal(L/K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the fundamental identification between ideal class group and Galois group for the unramified class field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.12 (Classification theorem for unramified abelian extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bijection between unramified abelian extensions M/K and subgroups H of Cl(OK); if M corresponds to H then Artin induces Cl(OK)/H ≅ Gal(M/K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives correspondence between intermediate unramified abelian extensions and subgroups of the class group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 3.13 (Dirichlet density)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S a set of finite primes of K, the Dirichlet density δ(S) = lim_{s→1+} (Σ_{p∈S} N(p)^{-s}) / (−log(s−1)), provided the limit exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic property: δ(S) > 0 implies S is infinite. Used to state Čebotarev density theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.14 (Čebotarev Density Theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L/K be Galois and σ ∈ Gal(L/K) with conjugacy class [σ] of size c. Let S be the set of finite primes p of K unramified in L with Frob_p = [σ]. Then δ(S) = c / |Gal(L/K)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives precise density of primes with prescribed Frobenius conjugacy class; implies existence of infinitely many such primes when density>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3.15 (abelian case density)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L/K is abelian and p a modulus divisible by ramified primes, then for any σ ∈ Gal(L/K) the set S of primes p not dividing m with Frob_p = σ has Dirichlet density δ(S) = 1/[L:K].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthens surjectivity of Artin map: every element of Gal(L/K) is achieved by infinitely many prime ideals p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of the ring class field
rubrics_metrics.description: For O an order of conductor f in imaginary quadratic K, Cl(O) ≅ I^f_K / P^f_{K,Z}. By Takagi there is a unique abelian extension L/K (ring class field) ramified only at primes dividing f OK, with Cl(O) ≅ Gal(L/K) and degree [L:K] = h(O).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ring class fields generalize the Hilbert class field (maximal order case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adeles, ideles and id`ele class group (Definition 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adele of K is x = (x_v) ∈ ∏_v K_v with |x_v|_v ≤ 1 for almost all v; the adeles form ring A_K. An id`ele is a unit in A_K; id`eles A^*_K = ∏'_v K_v^* with restricted product. The id`ele class group is C_K = A^*_K / K^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Idelic language gives global formulation of class field theory and convenient topological structure; A^*_K = (A^*_K)_f × (A^*_K)_inf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm maps on id`eles (Definition 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite extension L/K, NL/K: A^*_L → A^*_K is defined via normal closure M and product over σ ∈ Gal(M/K): NL/K(α) = ∏_σ σ(α) (well-defined in A^*_K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Norm groups NL/K(C_L) appear as kernels of Artin maps in idelic formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.3 (id`elic formulation of local Artin map)
rubrics_metrics.description: For abelian extension L/K there is a surjective map F_{L/K}: C_K → Gal(L/K) with ker(F_{L/K}) = NL/K(C_L), hence Gal(L/K) ≅ C_K / NL/K(C_L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes finite abelian extensions by norm subgroups of id`ele class group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.4 (Global Existence Theorem in idelic language)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bijection between finite abelian extensions L/K and closed subgroups of finite index in C_K given by L ↦ NL/K(C_L). The associated L is called the class field of the subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recasts Takagi existence in idelic/topological language: finite index closed subgroups ↔ finite abelian extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence subgroups of id`ele class group (Definition 4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For modulus m define (A^*_K)^m = ∏_p U_p^{n_p} and the congruence subgroup C^m_K = (A^*_K)^m K^*/K^* ⊂ C_K. The quotient C_K / C^m_K is the ray class group mod m; mod 1 gives the ideal class group I(OK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congruence subgroups provide the link between classical ray class groups and idelic closed subgroups; ray class fields correspond to these subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.6 (norm groups contain congruence subgroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed subgroups N of C_K of finite index (norm groups) are precisely those subgroups containing a congruence subgroup C^m_K for some modulus m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus every finite-index closed subgroup arises from classical congruence data and yields a ray class field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.1 (elliptic function for a lattice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given lattice Λ ⊂ C, an elliptic function for Λ is a meromorphic function f on C with f(z+ω) = f(z) for all ω ∈ Λ (i.e. doubly periodic and meromorphic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lattices Λ = [ω1, ω2]; elliptic functions have periods forming Λ; basic objects for complex multiplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass ℘-function and its fundamental properties (Proposition 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ℘-function generates elliptic functions; duplication and rationality relations show ℘(nz) rational in ℘(z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 5.3 (elliptic functions as rational functions in ℘ and ℘')
rubrics_metrics.description: Any elliptic function for Λ can be written as a rational function in ℘(z) and ℘'(z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies field of elliptic functions is C(℘,℘').

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminant ∆(Λ) and non-vanishing (Proposition 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ∆(Λ) = g2(Λ)^3 − 27 g3(Λ)^2 (related to cubic discriminant). Then ∆(Λ) ≠ 0 for any lattice Λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the cubic in x,y describing the elliptic curve has distinct roots; underlies definition of j-invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.5 (j-invariant of a lattice)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: j(Λ) is invariant under homothety and classifies complex tori up to isomorphism; singular moduli arise from lattices coming from ideals of imaginary quadratic orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.6 (j-characterizes lattices up to homothety)
rubrics_metrics.description: j(Λ) = j(Λ') iff Λ and Λ' are homothetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus j gives a complete invariant of complex elliptic curves/lattices modulo scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.7 (j-function on upper half plane)
rubrics_metrics.description: For τ ∈ H define j(τ) := j(Λ_τ) where Λ_τ = [1, τ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates lattice invariant to holomorphic function on upper half-plane with modular properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.8 (characterization of complex multiplication via ℘(αz) rationality)
rubrics_metrics.description: For lattice Λ and α ∈ C  ackslash Z, the following are equivalent: (i) ℘(αz) is a rational function in ℘(z). (ii) αΛ ⊂ Λ. (iii) There is an order O in an imaginary quadratic field K such that α ∈ O and Λ is homothetic to a proper fractional ideal of O. Moreover, ℘(αz) = A(℘(z))/B(℘(z)) with deg A = deg B + 1 = [Λ : αΛ] = N(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies nontrivial complex multiplications with orders in imaginary quadratic fields; explains terminology 'complex multiplication'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 5.9 (CM lattices and ideal class groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: For order O in imaginary quadratic field K, there is a bijection between ideal class group Cl(O) and homothety classes of lattices having O as their full ring of complex multiplications; in particular h(O) counts such homothety classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects arithmetic of orders to geometry of lattices and singular moduli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples: singular moduli j-values (Examples 5.10 and 5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: CM by i gives (up to homothety) Λ = [1,i], g3(Λ)=0 and j(i)=1728. CM by ω = e^{2πi/3} gives g2(Λ)=0 and j(ω)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete singular moduli illustrating extremal j-values for orders with extra automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.12 (basic properties of j(τ))
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) j(τ) is holomorphic on H. (ii) j(τ)=j(τ') iff τ' = γτ for some γ∈SL2(Z). (iii) j:H→C is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: j is the principal SL2(Z)-modular function, classifying lattices up to SL2(Z) action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.13 (modular function for Γ0(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: A modular function for Γ0(m) is meromorphic on H, invariant under Γ0(m) and meromorphic at all cusps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cusps correspond to Γ0(m)-equivalence classes in P^1(Q); meromorphic at infinity is expressed via q-expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.14 (q-expansion of j(τ))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The q-expansion has integer coefficients with no common factor; the 1728 normalization ensures integral coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.15 (modular functions for Γ0(m) generated by j(τ), j(mτ))
rubrics_metrics.description: j(τ) and j(mτ) are modular functions for Γ0(m), and every modular function for Γ0(m) is a rational function of j(τ) and j(mτ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete description of function field of modular curve X_0(m) in terms of j and its m-multiple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 5.16 (holomorphic modular functions for SL2(Z))
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) A holomorphic modular function for SL2(Z) which is holomorphic at infinity is constant. (ii) A holomorphic modular function for SL2(Z) is a polynomial in j(τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects that j generates the field of modular functions for SL2(Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 5.17 (modular polynomial Φ_m(X,Y))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Γ0(m) right coset representatives γ_i, define Φ_m(X,τ) = ∏_{i∈C(m)} (X − j(mγ_iτ)). The coefficients are SL2(Z)-invariant holomorphic functions and hence polynomials in j(τ); thus Φ_m(X,Y) ∈ C[X,Y] and Φ_m(X,j(τ)) = ∏_{σ∈C(m)} (X − j(σ τ)). Equation Φ_m(X,Y)=0 is the modular equation and Φ_m the modular polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed via values j(στ) for σ in C(m); encodes relations between j(τ) and j(mτ) and is central to explicit CM computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 5.18 (arithmetic properties of modular polynomial Φ_m)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Φ_m(X,Y) ∈ Z[X,Y]. (ii) Φ_m(X,Y) is irreducible as polynomial in X. (iii) Φ_m(X,Y) = Φ_m(Y,X) if m>1. (iv) For prime p, Φ_p(X,Y) ≡ (X^p − Y)(X − Y^p) (mod p Z[X,Y]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key integrality, symmetry, irreducibility and mod p factorization properties used in CM theory and reduction modulo primes.
